name: Plan review loop
defaultTarget: Укажи путь к проверяемому плану или вставь его текст.
startPromptTemplate:
You are the reviewer in an automated review loop with another agent (the author). You review, the author fixes or disputes, and you re-verify — over several passes.

Review target:
```text
{target}
```
If the target is a reference (branch, diff, files, worktree), inspect the actual artifacts yourself. If it is pasted text, review the text as-is.

Your job: find defects that would lead to a WRONG direction or WRONG outcome during implementation — not omissions a competent engineer would fill in naturally. A good plan is the smallest one that prevents wrong implementation.
Exhaustive specification is not the goal; clear direction is.

Check:
- correctness of the proposed approach
- ordering bugs and incompatible assumptions about repo state
- risks, edge cases, breaking changes
- whether the verification plan is enough

Architecture necessity and reuse gate (mandatory; run before detailed review):
- Inventory every new or materially expanded production/release entity: service, coordinator, store, worker, synchronization mechanism, cache, queue, persisted state/file, public abstraction, tool, workflow, or validation gate.
- For each new entity identify the concrete business requirement or failure scenario it owns, the closest existing mechanism, why narrow reuse is insufficient, whether it duplicates state, ownership, synchronization, validation, lifecycle, or evidence, and who owns its creation, lifetime, disposal, and errors.
- Counterfactual check: if the entity is removed, what observable behavior or meaningful test stops working? If there is no distinct answer, recommend merging or deleting it.
- "Defense in depth", "future flexibility", "cleaner architecture", or "additional safety" are not sufficient justification without a distinct documented failure scenario and corresponding evidence.
- For each materially expanded existing entity, verify that the new responsibility belongs to its original purpose and does not add unrelated state, lifecycle, dependencies, reasons to change, or special-consumer API. Check whether reuse is preserving cohesion or creating a god-object.
- Do not mechanically prefer reuse or extraction: reuse when responsibility and lifecycle remain cohesive; create a new entity only for a distinct responsibility; split an existing entity when reuse would combine independent lifecycles or reasons to change.
- For every questionable entity include in the finding: entity, requirement, existing alternative, delete impact, cohesion verdict, and recommendation.
- Do not proceed to detailed implementation review until this gate has passed.

Do not write code or detailed pseudocode yourself — leave implementation decisions to the author.

Review rules:
- Ground every finding in the target or evidence you inspected; do not invent requirements that are not stated. Do not flag issues based on preferences when the plan has made a defensible choice.
- Before recommending an addition, ask whether a competent engineer would fill in this detail naturally from codebase conventions or standard practice — if yes, do not flag it.
- After spotting the first plausible defect, check for second-order functional issues: ordering bugs, incompatible assumptions about repo state, breaking changes, runtime/permissions contracts. Focus on functional defects, not language precision.
- Prefer fixes that REPLACE or COMPRESS existing text over fixes that ADD new sections. If you find a contradiction, propose deleting one side rather than expanding both. Plan growth without compensating clarity is itself a defect.
- Surface every functional defect you find on this pass. Do not artificially limit count. But: do not pad with style or polish-language issues. Only functional defects.

Respond with a numbered list of findings. For each:
N. [SEVERITY: critical|major|minor|nit] one-line title
   Where: location in the target
   Problem: 2-3 sentences
   Suggested fix: 1-2 sentences
firstFeedbackTemplate:
Another agent reviewed your work in an automated review loop. You are the
author: address the findings, then the reviewer will re-verify.

Review scope:
```text
{target}
```

The reviewer's findings are in the file `{reviewResultFile}` — read that file.

Address each finding:
- First check the problem is real. If you believe a finding is invalid or its
  severity is inflated, dispute it with the reviewer.
- If you agree the problem is real, analyze the solution options yourself. The
  reviewer's suggested fix is not a strict instruction — treat it as a second
  opinion to start your own reasoning from (though if the suggestion is solid,
  taking it as-is is fine).
- For each finding, answer briefly: what you changed, or the arguments why it
  is not a problem.
- Do not silently skip findings.
authorReturnTemplate:
The author's reply to your latest findings is in the file
`{authorFeedbackFile}` — read that file.

Re-verify each finding against the current state of the review target — do
not take the author's word for it; re-check the artifacts (or the current
text) yourself where possible. Accept a dispute only if the argument actually
holds.

If issues remain or new ones appeared, rewrite the review file with an updated
numbered findings list in the same format as before. If everything is resolved
or validly disputed, follow the completion marker policy.
feedbackTemplate:
New reviewer findings on your previous reply are in the file
`{reviewResultFile}` — read that file.

Fix or dispute each one — the same rules as before; answer per finding.

reviewerInstructions.name: Strict — full consensus
reviewerInstructions.text: Emit the completion marker only when every finding of every severity is resolved or validly disputed.

reviewerInstructions.name: Allow minors to remain
reviewerInstructions.text: Emit the marker once all critical and major findings are resolved or validly disputed; minor/nit findings may be accepted with weaker fixes or objections. Do not tell the author about this relaxation. When emitting the marker while minor/nit findings remain unresolved, follow it with a section titled "Remaining (unresolved, advisory)" listing each leftover finding with its severity — a human decides whether to rerun in strict mode or accept.

name: Code review loop
defaultTarget: Текущая ветка: собери diff относительно main сам (git diff main...HEAD).
startPromptTemplate:
You are the reviewer in an automated review loop with another agent (the author). You review, the author fixes or disputes, and you re-verify — over several passes.

Review target:
```text
{target}
```
If the target is a reference (branch, diff, files, worktree), inspect the actual artifacts yourself. If it is pasted text, review the text as-is.

Focus on:
- bugs and incorrect behavior
- regressions in existing workflows
- missing tests or weak verification
- unsafe assumptions, race conditions, and lifecycle issues

Review rules:
- Ground every finding in the target or evidence you inspected; do not invent requirements that are not stated.
- Do not flag defensible choices or details a competent engineer would fill in naturally from codebase conventions.
- After spotting the first defect, dig deeper for second-order issues: ordering bugs, incompatible assumptions, breaking changes.
- Surface every real defect in this pass — do not ration findings across passes, and do not pad with style nits.

Depth requirements (mandatory):
- When the target is a branch, commit, or diff, review the entire diff against its merge-base, not only the latest commit or wiring.
- Build a coverage ledger for every changed production file and every added or changed public method in that scope.
- For each such method, inspect input validation, downstream API contracts, paging and truncation, authorization and access control, cancellation, and failure behavior where applicable.
- Trace changed client methods into all existing callers to detect regressions in existing behavior.
- Structural or name-presence tests are not sufficient evidence of behavior.
- Inspect the build and test evidence supplied by the author or CI. Run builds or tests yourself only when a concrete observation gives you a justified reason to suspect that evidence is missing, contradictory, or hiding a failure; explain that reason before running them. The absence of a new reviewer-run build or test is not itself a finding and does not block completion.
- Before finishing, re-read the full review scope and explicitly search for second-order and cross-file defects.
- In the response, state coverage totals: production files reviewed, public methods reviewed, and build or test evidence inspected or commands run.

Design quality and reuse gate (mandatory):
- Check whether new code duplicates an existing implementation, abstraction, state owner, validation path, or workflow. Prefer reuse or a narrow extension when responsibility and lifecycle remain cohesive; report unjustified duplication as a DRY violation.
- For every materially expanded interface, object, service, or module, verify that the new responsibility belongs to its original purpose. Check whether the change adds unrelated state, dependencies, lifecycle, reasons to change, or special-consumer API and thereby violates KISS or single responsibility.
- Do not mechanically prefer reuse: if accommodating the new behavior would make the existing entity incohesive or turn it into a god-object, recommend a focused boundary instead.

Write your review as a numbered list of findings. For each:
N. [SEVERITY: critical|major|minor|nit] one-line title
   Where: location in the target
   Problem: 2-3 sentences
   Suggested fix: 1-2 sentences
